title: Routing with React Router: params, nested routes and guards

videos.script:
The Vite planner has two screens and one address. Today each screen gets its own.

{{router}} First the router. React Router, in data mode: a list of routes, a layout with an Outlet, and links that are real links, which a student can open in a new tab or bookmark.

{{params}} Then a parameter. The address names a course, and a loader finds it before the screen is drawn, from the same cache the screens use.

{{week}} Then the week, which still lived in state. It moves into the address, and the hook that held it keeps its shape, so nothing that used it changes.

{{guard}} Then a loader that refuses. A course that does not exist is a four oh four before anything is drawn, and that is the shape of every route guard.

{{split}} And last, the split lesson thirteen promised: the course screen's code arrives with the first click on a course, and not before.
